newsitem.title: FRANCE: France Telecom funds to help cut state deficit.
newsitem.headline: France Telecom funds to help cut state deficit.

text.p: Funds due from France Telecom next year will be counted as state revenue, boosting the French government's chances to cut the budget deficit to three percent of gross domestic product, senior government officials said.
They said, however, that the funds, totalling 37.5 billion francs, will not be used to finance current spending.
France Telecom is due to transfer the funds to the state when it assumes its pension liabilities ahead of its partial privatisation.
Officials said the money would be counted as a revenue when it came to calculating France's total public deficit.

The government has pledged to reduce the total public deficit -- which includes the central government budget, welfare spending, local authority spending and a range of other state accounts -- to three percent of GDP next year.
